data_fields.name: row odds mode
data_fields.donor_constant: uniform, or peaked 2d((n+1)/2)-2 when n is odd and header is 2

data_fields.name: tier progression
data_fields.donor_constant: lmrvvvvv (L to M to R to V, V stays)

data_fields.name: stack count range
data_fields.donor_constant: RAND(1, N) inclusive, N from item*N suffix

data_fields.name: gold amount
data_fields.donor_constant: number in the entry (fixed, no roll)

data_fields.name: gold second charge
data_fields.donor_constant: uniform 0 to U-1 added to gold (IWD comment)

data_fields.name: treasure sub-table count
data_fields.donor_constant: up to 5 sub-tables from the difficulty column

best_idea: Give a loot row an upgrade that moves a chest to the next tier table (L to M to R to V), and resolve the whole nested table on the server in one pass capped at ten hops.
decision_why: Keep the row table with an explicit odds field, the tier-upgrade step, a ten-pass cap and a stack count range, resolved on the server at the verified kill. Reject resolution at record read or spawn time, the string grammar, the gold second-charge trick and the global difficulty column, which conflict with server-verified kills and zones as data.
acceptance: Server test with a seeded RNG: a three-row table with triangular odds gives about 25 / 50 / 25 over 100k kills (within 1 point); a chest row UP on table chest_l yields chest_m's pick, and on chest_v yields chest_v's pick; a nested table resolves to an item within ten hops; a zone with a missing table fails at load, not at the kill.
